title: RAW UNREVIEWED: repeated-base preference beyond marginal chunks and local seam constraints
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_EXECUTED. GDT1200 records literal BBdy wholes across several bases but did not measure whether identical halves are overrepresented relative to available unlike halves. Consider one descriptive conditional pairing comparison preserving half-length, separate left/right inventories and local seam constraints. A positive result could prioritize a repeated-base construction for further evidence; it cannot select a copying instruction, morpheme, meaning or source language. Null adequacy and exchangeability are unresolved; do not implement by default.

design.positive_anchor: GDT1200: alaldy, chchdy, ololdy; daldaldy has a material reader split. GDT1198 preserves exact standalone daldy and its nineteen-locus union separately.
design.question: Is exact within-group half identity an additional observed preference after controlling marginal chunk availability and short-range seam constraints?
design.candidate_unit: Complete literal dy-final raw group with an even-length preceding string split into equal-length U and V. This is only one analytical split, not a native segmentation. Retain each reading separately and all eligible unlike U,V controls; do not pool separated groups with fused groups.
design.candidate_comparison: Conditional reassignment of V among U within prespecified length, register/hand and seam strata, preserving left and right marginal inventories. Exact source contract, boundary eligibility, type/token weighting, strata and capacity rules are not frozen.
design.manual_objection: A shuffle unconstrained at the seam destroys known word-building restrictions. A seam-constrained shuffle may fix the observed self-pairs and offer no comparison capacity. Neither outcome may be repaired by changing conditioning after inspection.
design.identification_limit: Even an excess need not be a productive copying operation: learned whole words, an unmodelled higher-order spelling constraint and content-dependent lexical choices remain rivals. Existing GDT608 pair-specific residuals are not new evidence for a repeat command.
design.decision_requirement: Before implementation, show that an adequate prespecified contrast could change which concrete writer mechanism is pursued. If only broad ordered-composition dependence is rediscovered, do not run. No current selection or wall-time budget for implementation.
